source_documents.title: Multifunctional AIE-ESIPT dual mechanism tetraphenylethene-based Schiff base for inkless rewritable paper and colorimetric/fluorescent dual-channel Zn2+ sensor

reference_evidence_units.quote: The 410 nm emission band is attributed to the enol form of TPESB while the longer emission peak at 590 nm can be ascribed to its keto form resulted from the ESIPT reaction.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB
reference_evidence_units.statement: Enol and ESIPT keto bands; 265 nm Stokes shift.

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, when large amount of water was added (90%), the weak emission was significantly increased (about 10 times).
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB

reference_evidence_units.quote: Secondly, the free rotation of benzene rings will largely consume excited state energy through non-radiative channel, which will quench the emission seriously.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB
reference_evidence_units.statement: Free phenyl rotation quenches emission in solution.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Secondly, addition of water may lead to formation of aggregates, which will inhibit non-radioactive decay by restricted intramolecular rotation (RIR).
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB
reference_evidence_units.statement: Aggregation restricts rotation (aggregates confirmed by scattering, SEM).

reference_evidence_units.quote: Firstly, the photoinduced electron transfer (PET) effect can significantly quench the emission of TPESB.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB
reference_evidence_units.statement: PET proposed as a quenching route.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Cited from literature; no energetics or control for TPESB.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The chelation effect will restrict the PET effect and prevent the ESIPT
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPESB-Zn complex
reference_evidence_units.statement: Zn chelation blocks PET and ESIPT.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Free phenyl rotation quenches the solution; aggregation restricts it (RIR).

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Enol/keto emission from ESIPT; 'AIE-ESIPT dual mechanism' in the title.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: PET is invoked as a quenching route in solution, which water H-bonding is said to restrict. Weak: cited, no energetics or control experiment.
